text.name: TextDesc2
text.text: The Amstrad PCW (Personal Computer Wordprocessor) was a family of Z80-based personal computers introduced in 1985 and designed primarily for word processing and office productivity. Unlike the Amstrad CPC series, the PCW was supplied as a complete package including a monochrome monitor, keyboard, floppy disk drive, printer, and the CP/M operating system. Bundled with the Locoscript word processor, it offered an affordable all-in-one solution that quickly became popular with home users, schools, writers, and small businesses. Later models added larger memory configurations, dual floppy drives, and support for additional CP/M software, including programming languages, spreadsheets, and databases. Although intended as a dedicated business machine, the PCW also developed a modest library of games and productivity applications. Selling around eight million units across its lifetime, the PCW became one of the most successful word-processing computers ever produced and remains a landmark in affordable personal computing.
